usageNotes: Retrieves firewall log entries for a specific LXC container; useful for auditing traffic, diagnosing dropped packets, or confirming that firewall rules are matching as expected. The caller must have VM.Console permission on the container's /vms/{vmid} path. Use `since`/`until` (UNIX epoch integers) to narrow results to a time window, and `start`/`limit` for pagination through large logs.

examples.summary: Fetch the 50 most recent firewall log lines for container 110, filtered to the last hour

tips: Each returned object has 'n' (line number) and 't' (raw log text); parse 't' to extract action, interface, source/destination IP and port.
Firewall logging must be enabled on the container's firewall rules (log level != nolog) — this endpoint returns nothing if no rules are set to log.
For high-traffic containers, always supply `limit` to avoid pulling thousands of lines in a single call; paginate with `start` offsets.
Log entries reflect the host-level nftables/iptables kernel log, so timestamps are in local node time — correlate against node timezone when comparing across cluster nodes.
